title: Laser Light-Based Opacitometer ‘Peira LLBO 180’: A new and validated opacitometer for use in the Bovine Corneal Opacity and Permeability (BCOP) eye irritation test method
author: Van Rompay, Adriaens, et al.
materials: ○Remove the window-locking ring and glass window from all appropriate anterior chambers and place the corneas into a horizontal position (anterior chamber facing up).○Add test chemical to each chamber successively at a constant rate between each chamber. Apply approximately 0.75 mL of the control or test chemical (or enough test chemical to completely cover the cornea) directly to the epithelial surface of the cornea using a micropipettor or other appropriate device, such as a spatula. Maintain the corneas in a horizontal position (anterior chamber up).○If necessary, to aid in filling the pipette with test chemicals that are viscous, the test article may first be transferred to a syringe. Insert the pipette tip of the positive displacement pipette into the dispensing tip of the syringe, so that the test chemical can be loaded into the displacement tip under pressure. Simultaneously, depress the syringe plunger as the pipette piston is drawn upwards. If air bubbles appear in the pipette tip, the test chemical should be expelled and the process repeated until the tip is filled without air bubbles. This method should be used for any substances that cannot be easily drawn into the pipette (e.g. gels, toothpastes, and face creams).○If necessary, immediately upon dosing, slightly tilt the holders to achieve a uniform application of the test article over the entire cornea.○After all the chambers are dosed, replace the glass windows and window-locking rings.○Incubate the corneas in a horizontal position at 32 ± 1 °C for 10 ± 1 min. If other exposure incubation times are used, justification should be provided.○Prior to the end of the exposure period, remove the window-locking ring and glass window from each appropriate chamber.○At the completion of the exposure period, successively rinse each cornea in the exposure group according to the intervals that they were dosed. Using a syringe, add fresh complete MEM to the inside wall of the anterior chamber creating a “whirlpool or vortex effect”, which causes the test article to be rinsed off the cornea. Take special care not to spray the medium directly onto the cornea. Residual test article that cannot be removed from the cornea by the “whirlpool method” is removed by placing a layer of medium over the cornea (added to the inside wall of the chamber). Spray a gentle stream of medium through the medium layer, directing it towards the residual test item. If after several tries the test article cannot be removed, document this, and proceed to the next step.○Once each cornea is completely rinsed of test chemical, replace the glass window and window-locking ring. Continue rinsing as stated previously for the “closed chamber method”.○Observe each cornea visually and, if applicable, record pertinent observations (e.g. dissimilar opacity patterns, tissue peeling or residual test article).○Incubate the corneas in a vertical (anterior chamber facing forward) position at 32 ± 1 °C for 120 ± 10 min. If other post-exposure incubation times are used, justification should be provided.○Replace the medium in the anterior and posterior chamber with fresh complete MEM.

steps.title: Prepare test chemical solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare all test chemical solutions (substances and mixtures) fresh on the day of use according to the appropriate preparation method.

steps.title: Expose corneas to non‑viscous liquids
steps.instruction: Apply non‑viscous or slightly viscous test items to corneas, incubate, rinse, and post‑incubate as described.

substeps.instruction: Add 0.75 mL of the control or test chemical to the anterior chamber through the dosing holes using a micropipettor.
Reseal the dosing holes with the chamber plugs.
Rotate the holders so the corneas are horizontal; gently tilt back and forth to ensure uniform coverage of the cornea.
Incubate the corneas in the horizontal position at 32 ± 1 °C for 10 ± 1 min (any other exposure time must be justified).

Remove the chemical through the dosing holes and rinse the epithelium at least three times with approximately 2–3 mL fresh complete MEM using a syringe (and needle); perform one final rinse with fresh complete MEM. If visible chemical remains, document the observation. Refill the anterior chamber with fresh complete MEM and refresh the medium in the posterior chamber.
Observe each cornea visually and record any opacity patterns, tissue peeling, or residual test article.
Incubate the holders in a vertical position (anterior chamber facing forward) at 32 ± 1 °C for 120 ± 10 min (any other post‑exposure time must be justified).
Replace the medium in both the anterior and posterior chambers with fresh complete MEM.

steps.title: Expose corneas to viscous liquids
steps.instruction: Apply semi‑viscous or viscous test items to corneas using the closed‑chamber method, rinse, and post‑incubate as described.

substeps.instruction: Remove the window‑locking ring and glass window from each appropriate anterior chamber and place the corneas horizontal (anterior chamber facing up).

Add test chemical to each chamber successively at a constant rate, applying approximately 0.75 mL (or enough to completely cover the cornea) directly to the epithelial surface using a micropipettor or an appropriate device such as a spatula; keep corneas horizontal.

If the chemical is viscous, first transfer it to a syringe, insert the tip of a positive‑displacement pipette into the syringe’s dispensing tip, depress the syringe plunger while drawing the pipette piston upward to load the chemical under pressure. If air bubbles appear, expel the liquid and repeat until the tip is bubble‑free. Use this method for gels, toothpastes, face creams, etc.
If needed, immediately after dosing, slightly tilt the holders to achieve uniform coverage of the cornea.
After all chambers are dosed, replace the glass windows and window‑locking rings.
Incubate the corneas in the horizontal position at 32 ± 1 °C for 10 ± 1 min (any other exposure time must be justified).
Prior to the end of the exposure period, remove the window‑locking ring and glass window from each chamber.

At the end of exposure, rinse each cornea sequentially according to its dosing interval: using a syringe, add fresh complete MEM to the inside wall of the anterior chamber to create a “whirlpool” or vortex effect that rinses the test article off the cornea. Avoid spraying medium directly onto the cornea. If residual test article remains, add a layer of medium over the cornea, then spray a gentle stream of medium through this layer toward the residue. If the residue still cannot be removed after several attempts, document the observation and proceed.
Once each cornea is completely rinsed, replace the glass window and window‑locking ring and continue rinsing as described for the closed‑chamber method.
Observe each cornea visually and record any opacity patterns, tissue peeling, or residual test article.
Incubate the corneas in a vertical position (anterior chamber facing forward) at 32 ± 1 °C for 120 ± 10 min (any other post‑exposure time must be justified).
Replace the medium in both the anterior and posterior chambers with fresh complete MEM.
